newsitem.title: HUNGARY: EGIS SEES SALES UP 20 PERCENT IN 1997.
newsitem.headline: EGIS SEES SALES UP 20 PERCENT IN 1997.

text.p: Hungarian pharmaceuticals company Egis Gyogyszergyar Rt said on Friday it planned to boost its turnover to 30 billion forints in 1997 and sees its profits growing to 6.3 billion.
"The (business) plan calls for a 20 percent increase in turnover," Egis said in its earnings report.
"Within this, we expect domestic sales to rise 16 percent (of this 11 percent by price rises), while exports to grow by 33 percent (14 percent in dollar terms)," Egis said.

The company, majority-owned by France's Servier S.A., said it planned to boost its trading and marketing expenditures by more than 60 percent in 1997. "As a result, the pre-tax profit is expected to rise by 14 percent."
"The substantial material and marketing expenditures will lay the foundations of a rapid increase in turnover and profits in the coming years," Egis said.

The company released its preliminary 1996 results this morning and reported its after-tax profit rising to 5.58 billion forints on net sales of 24.69 billion forints against an after-tax profit of 4.84 billion forints on sales of 19.81 billion in 1995.
Egis said that in 1996 its total exports grew by four percent (in dollar terms) to $74.1 million but its sales to eastern Europe exceeded this pace.
"Within the exports its worth to emphasise the turnover growth in eastern Europe, which shows a 16 percent growth in dollar terms," Egis said.
Of total 1996 sales domestic sales amounted to 13.62 billion, while exports amounted to 11.07 billion forints.
